A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sundial, TimeFlow Loss, and TimeBench research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated results and showcases.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting results, training curves, training-objective comparisons, sampling analyses, and fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds architectural ablations, training-data scaling experiments, lookback-length analyses, and probabilistic comparisons of training objectives.

M1.justification: The patch tokenization, Transformer components, TimeFlow objective, model configurations, and sampling algorithm remain unchanged. The S3 terminology and explanation of sharing lookback representations expand the implementation description without establishing a new algorithm or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TimeBench sources and retain six TSLib datasets, 23 GIFT-Eval datasets, and 27 FEV datasets. The added data-subset and lookback experiments use existing coverage rather than introducing new tasks or domains.

E2.justification: GIFT-Eval Table 2 replaces VisionTS with TabPFN. Timer is relabeled Timer-XL in the point-forecasting tables, retaining the same cited work and numerical results; this does not establish a separately added comparator.

E3.justification: GIFT-Eval changes from 20 to 100 generated predictions; FEV retains 20 predictions and 50 sampling steps. Added evaluation designs compare training-data scales, lookback lengths, normalization at 15,000 versus 30,000 iterations, and CRPS across objectives. Table 6 also revises Timer-XL's reported size and maximum context, without establishing that its evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 adds ablations of RoPE, layer normalization, FlashAttention, and KV Cache. Appendices C.1-C.3 add probabilistic objective comparisons, data-scale controls, and lookback sensitivity. These substantially extend the existing objective, sampling, adaptation, and showcase analyses.

E5.justification: GIFT-Eval's predictive statistics are now estimated from 100 generated series instead of 20, changing the Monte Carlo sample count used for uncertainty estimation. FEV sampling and the showcase 80% prediction intervals remain unchanged. Neither version reports training-seed variability or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces Sundial's GIFT-Eval MASE/CRPS of 0.727/0.505 with 0.673/0.472 under changed sampling settings. FEV MASE/WQL changes from 0.845/0.712 to 0.834/0.694, and reported speedup over Chronos changes from 11.34-fold to 35-fold. Sampling and fine-tuning scores also change, and substantial ablation results are added. The full TSLib point-forecasting results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation, equations 1-9, and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears. The added ARMA analogy and mode-collapse discussion are qualitative explanations.

C1.justification: The central contributions—continuous generative forecasting through TimeFlow, trillion-point pre-training, scalability, and strong zero-shot performance—remain. The revised abstract adds the specific capability claim of forecasting within a few milliseconds and gives real-time inference greater prominence.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of architectural ablations and task-dependent lookback selection. Appendix E replaces the specific trend-underestimation example and uncertainty about its cause with a warning about very high-frequency data linked to TimeBench's frequency composition. Univariate-information and autoregressive oversmoothing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies code and model-checkpoint access information and reports releasing detailed benchmark results, whereas v1 only promises a future results release. It also specifies 32 A100 GPUs and adds preprocessing and shared-representation sampling details. These are substantial additions to documented reproducibility resources, whose external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: The reference set receives limited substantive updates, including TabPFN, Koopa, Baevski and Auli, LLaMA, and Vovk et al.; VisionTS, Ho et al., Zeng et al., and Angelopoulos and Bates are removed. The broader positioning around continuous tokenization and generative foundation models remains.

P1.justification: Existing passages throughout the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, inference discussion, and limitations are substantially rewritten. Model Inference becomes Test-Time Calibration, Appendix C is reorganized, and acknowledgements and a main-text impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel architectural-ablation figure, a lookback-length figure, and two supplementary result tables, while removing v1's evaluation-summary figure. Experimental displays are rearranged, axes and captions are revised, and the architecture diagram is refined. All five appendix showcase graphics are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added component ablations and comparisons using matched pre-training data strengthen support for the design and scaling claims, while code and checkpoint information improves reproducibility. These gains are tempered by reporting gaps: v2 gives GIFT-Eval CRPS as 0.472 in Table 2 and 0.5050 in Table 7 without explaining the setting difference, and retains the PatchTST-leading interpretation despite Table 2 favoring TimesFM.
